location: Tasks > tests ('a `fail` and an exit 2 reaped in one batch -> `fail-fast after …`, exit 2') vs Always > Fail-fast ('Children reaped in one batch are handled in plan order; the first trigger fixes the reason')
issue: The expected reason in this test only follows from the rule when the failing version comes before the exit-2 version in plan order. If the exit-2 version comes first, the first trigger is the exit 2 and the reason must be `input-error after <ver>`. The test line does not state the order. It also does not say how a test forces two children into one batch. The loop wakes on the first child exit, so with the `E2EChild` harness the two exits are normally reaped in two passes. That is only avoided if the loop is blocked, for example inside a stubbed `daemon_slot_usage` call while a third version is still queued, until both children have finished.
implementation_impact: The test author has to guess the plan order. With the opposite order, a correct implementation fails the written expectation. Without a blocking hook the 'one batch' case is racy, so the test can be flaky or can end up testing the two-batch path.
suggestion: State the order, e.g. `--cells 9.1:chromium,8.1:chromium,1.7.8:chromium` with 9.1 `fail` and 8.1 exit 2, which gives `fail-fast after 9.1:chromium` for 1.7.8 and run exit 2. Optionally add the mirror case (exit 2 first -> `input-error after 9.1`). Name the mechanism that forces one batch: a third queued version, and a stubbed `daemon_slot_usage` that returns only after both children have exited.

location: Design Notes > Records ('`rc=<child exit code>` after a reaped child (`rc=crash` when killed by a signal)') vs ps-run-layer.py `plan_children`/`_spawn` (children run as `uv run <script>`), `STOPPED_CODES = (143, -15)`, `run_children` (rc `None` when the runner raises)
issue: ps-run-layer never sees the Python child's own return code. It sees the return code of the `uv run` wrapper. A child killed by a signal usually comes back as a positive code from uv (for example 137 or 143), not as a negative `returncode`, so the `rc=crash` branch may never fire. The rule also covers neither `rc None` (the runner raised, e.g. `uv` missing from PATH), which today becomes a `crash` record, nor rc 143/-15. Those two codes are treated as 'stopped, no record' for the history, but they would get `DONE rc=143` or `DONE rc=crash` in the log when the child died before writing its own `DONE`.
implementation_impact: The implementer has to guess what counts as 'killed by a signal' (only rc < 0, or also 128+N) and what to write for `None`. The log line and the history can then disagree: the log says `crash` for a version whose history treats it as stopped, or `rc=None` appears in a contract token.
suggestion: Define the mapping completely: rc `None` -> `rc=crash`; rc in `STOPPED_CODES` -> `rc=stopped`; rc < 0, or rc > 128 when the child left no `DONE` -> `rc=crash`; otherwise `rc=<rc>`. Add one test that checks the DONE line for a SIGKILL-like code and one for `None`.

location: Always > Fail-fast ('A child exit 2 does the same with `input-error after <ver>`') + Tasks > docs (Run outcomes: '`input-error after …` once the rejected input is fixed') vs deferred-work.md entry 'ps-run-layer cannot tell `uv run`'s own exit 2 … from ps-e2e-run's input-error exit 2'
issue: A known, deferred defect gets a new consequence in this slice that the spec does not mention. `uv run` exits 2 on its own failures: resolve, cache, permission, or an env sync hiccup. Before this slice that only ended the E2E loop and appended nothing. Now it also appends a permanent `not-run` record with reason `input-error after <ver>` to the history of every queued cell, and the docs tell the operator to fix 'the rejected input', which does not exist.
implementation_impact: The implementer follows the rule as written. The resulting histories and docs then send Budi looking for a nonexistent input error after a transient uv failure. Nothing in the spec says this is accepted, so a reviewer may treat it as a defect of this slice.
suggestion: State that this is an accepted interim consequence. Add a docs sentence: an `input-error after …` with no rejected input in the child's stderr can be a `uv run` failure, so rerun the cell. Add an addendum line to the existing deferred-work entry noting that this slice now writes not-run records from such exits. Alternatively, have ps-run-layer require the child's `-o` file or a stderr marker before treating exit 2 as input-error, but that is a contract change and needs Ask First.

location: Design Notes > Claims ('Claims of every other registry entry whose `entry_state` is `alive`, plus the run's own claims held in memory (never re-read from its own file)') + Tasks > tests (harness runs `mod.main` in-process; `fl.job_register` + `atexit` unregister only the last entry)
issue: The spec does not say how ps-run-layer recognises its own registry entry when it skips it: by entry file path, by `pid == OWNER_PID`, or by job id. In production one process registers once, so all three readings agree. In the test harness, every `_run_full` call runs in the same test process. Each call registers a new job whose entry has the same pid and a `script` that matches the live cmdline, so `entry_state` reports earlier entries as `alive`, and `_job_unregister` (atexit) removes only the last one. If 'own' means 'my current entry path', a leftover entry from an earlier run in the same registry dir is counted as a foreign alive entry. Its leftover `slot_claims` (e.g. from a stop test, where claims of in-flight children are never removed) then fill the cap in later tests.
implementation_impact: Whether later tests wait or go `no-slots` depends on a choice the spec leaves open and on whether the harness uses a fresh `JOB_REGISTRY` for each run or for each test file. This kind of order-dependent flakiness is hard to trace.
suggestion: Say that every entry with `pid == fl.OWNER_PID` (same host, boot and ns) is this process and never counted. Or require the harness to point `JOB_REGISTRY` at a fresh temp dir for every `_run_full` call. Preferably do both.

location: Tasks > docs ('E2E commands use `--slots`'; 'the daemon-wide count checked against this run's own N (equal `psm_e2e_slots` everywhere gives one shared ceiling)') vs run-phases.md Fase 2 command (`--jobs <N>`) and interim-orchestration.md Fase 2 step 3 ('`--jobs` as today')
issue: The spec does not say whether the documented commands should pass `--slots <N>` explicitly, and with what N, or omit the flag and let `psm_e2e_slots` come from `--config <cfg>`. Today's template has a free `--jobs <N>`. A literal swap to `--slots <N>` invites a different ceiling per run, which defeats the 'one shared ceiling' the same sentence relies on.
implementation_impact: The docs writer has to guess the command shape. If the guess keeps a free `--slots <N>`, orchestrators in different sessions run with different N, and each run checks the shared daemon count against its own ceiling.
suggestion: Decide that the orchestrator commands omit `--slots` (the value comes from `psm_e2e_slots` in `<cfg>`), and that `--slots` is documented only as a manual override. Apply the same wording to interim-orchestration.md Fase 2 step 3.

location: Tasks > docs ('per-run advice such as `--jobs 1` or "lower `--jobs`" becomes one version per `--cells` call / lower `psm_e2e_slots`') vs run-phases.md 'Pantau run Docker' ('Macet berulang di `wait-healthy`/`bring-up` … turunkan `--jobs`'; 'Harness tanpa eksekusi latar … `--versions V` / `--cells V:…`, `--jobs 1`')
issue: Both run-phases.md passages are general: they cover Layer 2 and Layer 5 runs as well as E2E. `--jobs` stays the concurrency knob for Layers 2/5, and the contract never counts Layer 2/5 containers under `psm.slots`. Replacing the advice wholesale with 'lower `psm_e2e_slots`' removes the only Layer 2/5 guidance. It also suggests a fix that does not help when Layer 2/5 boots are what saturates the daemon.
implementation_impact: The docs writer either deletes valid Layer 2/5 advice or has to guess how to split it per layer.
suggestion: Split the advice per layer. For E2E: one version per `--cells` call, or a lower `psm_e2e_slots`. For Layers 2/5: `--versions V`, `--jobs 1`, or a lower `--jobs`. Also note that Layer 2/5 containers are not counted toward the E2E cap.

location: Design Notes > Claims ('Claims of every other registry entry whose `entry_state` is `alive`') + Acceptance Criteria #2 (seeded entry with 'no `script`') vs cell-contract.md > Config keys > `psm_e2e_slots` ('counts the `slot_claims` of every live ps-run-layer registry entry')
issue: The contract limits counted claims to ps-run-layer entries. The spec counts claims from any alive entry, and AC2 depends on that: its seeded entry has no `script`, so it is not recognisably a ps-run-layer entry. The spec says the contract is authoritative for the rules it names. An implementer who follows the contract literally and filters by `script == 'ps-run-layer.py'` or `layer == 'e2e'` makes AC2 fail. Writing back this kind of difference is what the spec's Ask First reserves for the human.
implementation_impact: The implementer has to choose between the contract text and the AC. Only ps-run-layer writes `slot_claims`, so the two rules behave the same in practice, but the reviewer may flag either choice.
suggestion: Write the wider rule back to cell-contract.md ('any live registry entry that carries `slot_claims`; only ps-run-layer writes them'). Alternatively, keep the contract wording and give the AC2 entry `script: "ps-run-layer.py"`, with a test subprocess whose cmdline contains that string.
